verdict.rationale: Supabase's branching feature (create/merge/reset/rebase branches) lets users version and review schema/config changes in isolated preview environments before merging to production, and the MCP toolset exposes migration tracking (list_migrations, apply_migration) plus branch tools that an AI agent can use to review and roll back changes; PITR/backups also allow rolling back the database to a point in time. However, this is schema/database-centric versioning, not a dedicated versioning/rollback system for 'automations' like Edge Functions, Cron jobs, or Webhooks. Missing for 10: explicit version history and rollback for deployed Edge Functions and Cron jobs, an audit/undo trail for AI-agent-triggered automation actions, and independent hands-on evidence of an agent actually reviewing/rolling back an automation via these tools.
